releases.body:
### Pause autonomous work in a shared project

* The Shared tab has **Pause work** / **Resume work** (durable
  `projects.work_paused`, with the actor and timestamp); the project card is
  badged `paused`. While paused the bridge posts no room replies, does not feed
  the room's messages to coroutine triggers, skips the autonomous proposal
  review, and policy auto-approve leaves new proposals pending. In-flight runs
  finish; human chat and explicit approvals remain available.
* Members can keep chatting: paused messages stay in room history for the agent
  to catch up after a resume. The bridge posts one notice per pause period so the
  room knows why the agent is silent.

### Resume skips machine-created sessions

* `GET /api/projects/{slug}/sessions` now reports `tui` per session: `true` when
  the session's **first** linked run was a TUI launch, `false` when it was a
  headless job, and `null` when there is no run evidence (manual/legacy). A later
  resume never flips a headless session into a chat.
* The card's main **Run** resumes the newest TUI/unknown session and starts a
  fresh one when only headless sessions exist. The caret picker and the Agent
  Console list every session with a `TUI chat` / `headless run` label, and the
  console default skips headless sessions.
* This keeps a machine session (including one created by an old run with a
  malformed instruction prompt) from being reopened as if it were the
  operator's chat.

### Follow-ups from the production audit

* A failed TUI launch now finishes the run record it created instead of leaving a
  phantom "working" card, and launches are single-flight per project, so a
  re-rendered card or a second click (including via the caret) cannot open two
  terminals.
* `Orchestrator.start_run()` enforces the same `session_pk` ownership rule as
  `/api/runs/tui`, so headless runs, MCP tools, Telegram and the project-session
  endpoint can no longer attach another project's usage.
* Focus caches its resolved window per `(pid, run_uid)`, so a recycled pid cannot
  raise another run's terminal.
* The coroutine Work step explains that editing a job keeps its already-composed
  task blocks; adding tasks appends new ones.

### Hardening for TUI session resume

* The card **Run** button disables while it looks up the newest session, so a
  double click cannot launch two terminals.
* `POST /api/runs/tui` rejects a `session_pk` that belongs to another project
  (400), so a crafted request cannot attach another project's usage.
* The Agent Console session picker skips sessions with no `opencode_session_id`,
  because such a session cannot be passed to `opencode --session`.

### Focus finds the terminal through its console again

* On Windows 11 the shell has no live process-tree link to Windows Terminal (the
  ConPTY host exits) and the tab title belongs to OpenCode, so Focus could report
  "no terminal window found" while the terminal was open — especially once the
  window showed another active tab or its title changed.
* Focus now asks the console itself: a short-lived detached helper attaches to the
  run's console and reads the console window, whose **owner** is the exact Windows
  Terminal window (a classic console owns its window directly). This is
  deterministic and needs no title, project name, or OpenCode service call; the
  existing window/title search remains the fallback.
* `ProcessTracker.run_terminal_pid()` falls back to the run row's persisted pid
  when the in-memory launcher handle has died (e.g. `wt.exe`) instead of reporting
  a live terminal as unattributable. Marker verification is unchanged.

### Project coroutines can include project tasks

* The coroutine wizard's **Work** step now lists the execution project's enabled
  tasks. Several can be selected at once, shown as removable chips, and composed
  with the optional extra prompt by `buildCoroutinePrompt`. A skill task becomes
  a structured instruction for the headless run, not a TUI slash command.
* The composed prompt is saved once; editing the project's tasks later does not
  rewrite an existing coroutine. A job with tasks and no extra prompt is valid.
* Quick create keeps its single-prompt shortcut; use **New coroutine** for task
  selection.

### Run resumes the latest TUI session

* The project card's main **Run** now resumes the latest OpenCode session for
  that project (`opencode --session <id>`) instead of always starting a new one.
  The caret next to it starts a **new** session or opens a picker of the
  project's existing sessions; a project with no sessions starts fresh.
* The Agent Console's session picker defaults to the latest session and keeps
  **New session** as the first, explicit choice. The TUI run record carries
  `opencode_session_id` and `session_pk`, so Finish captures that session's
  usage.
* **Stop is unchanged**: it closes the terminal Perun opened, ending every
  session in that terminal.

### Operator ask dedupe and inbox batching

* A mention is deduplicated by a fingerprint of room + sender + timestamp + text,
  so a replay under a fresh frame id cannot create a second inbox item. The
  operator's own handle is skipped, and settings/operator names are cached for
  30 s per message burst.
* `attention.reconcile_proposals()` now resolves proposal statuses in one query
  and closes cards in one transaction (`action_proposals.statuses`,
  `registry.close_attention_many`) instead of two connections per open card.
* Payload identities above 200 KB collapse to a short `len:<n>:<hash>` key, and
  the chat “operator asks” strip orders by the message timestamp rather than the
  inbox row id.

### Proposal cards leave the inbox when the proposal is decided

* `attention.reconcile_proposals()` — run by the watcher — closes an approval
  card once its proposal is `approved`/`claimed`/`executing`/`executed`,
  `rejected`, or no longer exists. The inbox and the proposal board can no longer
  disagree about what is still waiting, which was the root of the “nothing
  pending” reply while eleven approved proposals sat unexecuted.

### Operator asks are durable, structured messages are readable, proposals show expiry

* A room message that names the operator now creates a `room` attention item
  **even when Perun also answers**. The PerunChat page shows an “N operator asks
  for you” strip, and a new **Needs you** page (and nav entry) lists room
  mentions alongside permissions, forms, proposals and handoffs; replying there
  posts back to the exact room.
* Structured (object) room payloads render as an expandable JSON preview with a
  type/status summary and a proposal chip, instead of `[object Object]`. Object
  dedupe uses a real payload key, not `String(payload)`.
* Active proposals show their expiry in the peek, the Shared row and the chip
  tooltip. The proposal MCP tools now return `expires_at`, and the room persona
  treats `approved` (awaiting claim or execution) as pending — never “nothing
  pending” while an approved proposal has no executor.
